answer: Human Passport proved it: one score, many stamps. A vote here needs a kernel of credentials — GitHub history, ENS, Civic — totalling 20 points, minted on-chain, re-checked every 90 days. Ten thousand fakes hit one gate: Twitter and Google score 1 each, so cheap accounts never reach 20; only an aged GitHub history at 7.25 plus Civic at 6 count, and aged GitHub accounts sell from $48, so 10,000 cost $480,000, while the farm wanders the web re-earning them quarterly. Like onyx, identity forms only under years of pressure: a fake that cannot show it loses $480,000 and is rejected.
